title: The sky taxis with no pilots
titleChinese: 无人驾驶的空中出租车
paragraphs: You know that feeling. You‘re stuck in bumper-to-bumper traffic. It’s going to be hours before you get home. We all know that congestion is one of the downsides of modern city life. Don‘t you wish you could take to the skies and zoom above it all in a helicopter?

Well, wish no more. Right now, the race is on to release the first commercially viable sky taxi. No longer will personal air travel be the preserve of the super wealthy, say optimistic tech entrepreneurs. There’s just one catch: how do you feel about having no pilot?

For brave passengers, the city of Dubai plans to roll out rides on their pilotless drone taxi project by the end of this year. You can buckle up and share the ride with one other passenger in their 18-rotor craft, developed by German start-up Volocopter, with a top speed of 100km/h and a flight time of around 30 minutes.

If you have more friends, French aviation company Airbus are working on a drone which can carry four to six customers. Or if you prefer your own company, Chinese firm Ehang are pioneering a single-seater drone, which stays airborne for 23 minutes.

Ride-hailing company Uber also want a piece of the action. They say drones like this are the “future of on-demand urban air transportation”. They recently poached NASA chief technologist Mark Moore to help them develop a drone taxi. And he claims it won‘t cost the earth. Moore told the BBC that with three or four passengers sharing, it would be “very similar to what an UberX [car] costs today”.

So far so good. But naturally, a number of questions remain. On the technical side, there‘s the problem of batteries. A 23-minute flight could get you across town, but how and where does the battery recharge?

And regulations are a challenge too. US authorities require aircraft to carry at least 20 minutes of spare fuel. If you only have 23 or even 30 in total, that leaves very little leeway. Control of access to flight paths will also need to be worked out.

vocabulary.entry: bumper-to-bumper traffic [phr.] /ˌbʌmpə tə ˈbʌmpə ˈtræfɪk/ 交通拥堵；水泄不通的交通 (口语)

vocabulary.translation: 每项新技术都有其缺点。

vocabulary.translation: 这是解决这个问题的一个可行方案。

vocabulary.entry: preserve [n.] /prɪˈzɜːv/ 专属；独占的事物 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Fishing in this river used to be the preserve of local residents.
vocabulary.translation: 在这条河里捕鱼曾经是当地居民的专属。

vocabulary.entry: roll out [phr.] /rəʊl aʊt/ 推出；开展
vocabulary.example: The company will roll out its new product next month.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司下个月将推出新产品。

vocabulary.entry: buckle up [phr.] /ˈbʌkəl ʌp/ 系好安全带 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Please buckle up before the plane takes off.
vocabulary.translation: 飞机起飞前请系好安全带。

vocabulary.entry: pioneering [adj.] /ˌpaɪəˈnɪərɪŋ/ 开创性的；先驱的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The company made pioneering advances in electric vehicles.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司在电动汽车领域取得了开创性的进展。

vocabulary.entry: airborne [adj.] /ˈeəbɔːn/ 在空中飞行的；升空的
vocabulary.example: The plane was airborne within minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 飞机几分钟内就升空了。

vocabulary.entry: poached [v.] /pəʊtʃt/ 挖走（人才等）；偷猎 (原形: poach)
vocabulary.example: The tech giant poached several engineers from its rival.
vocabulary.translation: 这家科技巨头从竞争对手那里挖走了几名工程师。

vocabulary.entry: leeway [n.] /ˈliːweɪ/ 余地；回旋余地 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: We need to leave some leeway for unexpected delays.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要为意外延误留出一些余地。

vocabulary.entry: biggie [n.] /ˈbɪɡi/ 重要的事物；关键问题 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The battery life is a biggie for smartphone users.
vocabulary.translation: 电池续航对智能手机用户来说是个大问题。

vocabulary.entry: congestion [n.] /kənˈdʒestʃən/ 拥堵；拥挤
vocabulary.example: Congestion in the city centre is a daily problem.
vocabulary.translation: 市中心的拥堵是一个日常问题。

vocabulary.entry: helicopter [n.] /ˈhelɪkɒptə/ 直升机
vocabulary.example: The rescue team arrived by helicopter.
vocabulary.translation: 救援队乘直升机到达。

vocabulary.entry: entrepreneurs [n. pl.] /ˌɒntrəprəˈnɜːz/ 企业家 (单数: entrepreneur)
vocabulary.example: Young entrepreneurs are starting innovative businesses.
vocabulary.translation: 年轻的企业家正在创办创新型企业。

vocabulary.entry: rotor [n.] /ˈrəʊtə/ 旋翼；转子
vocabulary.example: The helicopter‘s rotor blades began to spin.
vocabulary.translation: 直升机的旋翼叶片开始旋转。

vocabulary.entry: aviation [n.] /ˌeɪviˈeɪʃən/ 航空；航空业
vocabulary.example: She works in the aviation industry.
vocabulary.translation: 她在航空业工作。

vocabulary.entry: on-demand [adj.] /ˌɒn dɪˈmɑːnd/ 按需的；随需应变的 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Streaming services offer on-demand entertainment.
vocabulary.translation: 流媒体服务提供按需娱乐。

vocabulary.entry: recharge [v.] /riːˈtʃɑːdʒ/ 给……充电；恢复精力
vocabulary.example: Don’t forget to recharge your phone before you leave.
vocabulary.translation: 出门前别忘了给手机充电。

vocabulary.entry: regulations [n. pl.] /ˌreɡjʊˈleɪʃənz/ 法规；条例 (单数: regulation)
vocabulary.example: The new safety regulations apply to all airlines.
vocabulary.translation: 新的安全法规适用于所有航空公司。

vocabulary.entry: tackle [v.] /ˈtækəl/ 解决；处理
vocabulary.example: The government needs to tackle the problem of pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 政府需要解决污染问题。
